title: 2026 global growth to slow to 2.5%, lowest since COVID-19: World Bank
summary:
The Iran war is expected to slow global growth to the lowest rate since the COVID-19 pandemic, the World Bank has said.
Global growth is forecast to slow to 2.5 per cent in 2026 from 2.9 per cent in 2025. 
Forecasts for two-thirds of economies have been downgraded relative to January 2026. 
This year, growth in developing economies is expected to drop to a post-pandemic low of 3.6 per cent.

title: South India cotton yarn continues to see sluggish demand, prices down
summary:
South India’s cotton yarn market remained under pressure as weak demand, labour shortages and slower downstream activity weighed on prices.
Mumbai yarn prices fell by ₹5–7 per kg, while Tiruppur remained stable but sluggish.
Cotton prices in Gujarat were steady, though bearish sentiment, weaker demand and lower CCI prices continued to discourage fresh buying.

title: Naphtha to yarn: Lower upstream reshapes cost
summary:
Brent and WTI crude have fallen sharply since mid-May, driving a broad petrochemical cost correction. 
Naphtha is down around 25 per cent, while benzene, propylene and acrylonitrile have softened, easing input costs across synthetic fibre chains. 
Nylon DTY has started to decline, acrylic staple fibre remains stable, and polyester yarn prices are range-bound as buyers and producers remain cautious.

title: World cotton supply-demand outlook may tighten next year: WASDE
summary:
USDA’s June WASDE report points to a tighter global cotton balance in 2026–27, with lower beginning and ending stocks and slightly higher consumption.
World production is forecast to remain stable at 116.04 million bales, while demand rises, led by China.
For 2025–26, stronger exports are expected to reduce global ending stocks and tighten supply further.

title: Strong export demand boosts US cotton sales and shipments
summary:
US cotton export demand strengthened in the week ended June 4, with Upland sales rising 12 per cent to 207,000 RB and shipments increasing 12 per cent to 300,100 RB.
Vietnam, Pakistan and India led buying.
New-crop Upland sales surged to 298,700 RB.
Pima shipments hit a marketing-year high of 22,900 RB, driven by strong demand from India and Pakistan.

title: EU unemployment rate edges up to 6% in 2025
summary:
The EU unemployment rate rose slightly to 6 per cent in 2025 from 5.9 per cent in 2024, according to Eurostat. 
Spain recorded the highest rate at 10.5 per cent, while Czechia had the lowest at 2.8 per cent. 
Unemployment remained strongly linked to education levels, with low-educated individuals facing a 10.5 per cent jobless rate, compared to 3.6 per cent among highly educated people.

title: Drewry WCI rises on higher rates on Transpacific, Asia-Europe routes
summary:
Drewry’s WCI rose 3.37 per cent to $3,549 per FEU, marking a sixth straight weekly gain, driven by stronger Transpacific and Asia-Europe freight rates.
Early peak-season demand, tariff-related frontloading, Red Sea disruptions and higher fuel costs are supporting rates.
Carriers have announced fresh surcharges, with further increases expected in the coming weeks.

title: Continued pressure on global supply chains in May: GEP-S&P Global
summary:
Global supply chains are much strained as manufacturers front-load purchasing to guard against expected higher prices in 2026 second half, S&P Global said.
Safety stockpiling, shortages and transportation costs have all been higher for three months in a row, a rare signal.
North America supply chain pressures have risen to their highest since August 2022.
Asia remains under the greatest strain globally.

title: ICE cotton bounces back on short covering, positive US reports
summary:
ICE cotton futures rebounded on technical short covering, strong US export sales and a supportive USDA WASDE report showing lower global ending stocks.
July futures settled at 72.49 cents/lb and December at 76.39 cents/lb.
Softer US inflation improved sentiment, but traders remain cautious as volatility is expected ahead of First Notice Day and options expiry.

title: Spain’s economy to significantly beat eurozone in 2026: Goldman Sachs
summary:
Spain’s economy is expected to significantly outpace the euro area in 2026 as it benefits from higher labour productivity and a strengthening fiscal position, Goldman Sachs Research said.
It is projected to raise its GDP by 2.1 per cent YoY, thrice the expected 0.7-per cent rise for the currency union.
Its unemployment rate has dropped to its lowest since 2008, and employment rate is at an all-time high.

title: China compliance wall raises proof over production in apparel sourcing
summary:
China’s 2026 compliance decrees are reshaping apparel sourcing by making supply-chain data harder to collect and transfer. 
As global traceability demands rise, competitive advantage will shift from low-cost production to verifiable proof of origin, labour and supplier links. 
China remains central to textile supply chains, making transparency (not relocation) the key sourcing challenge.

title: Bangladesh-Japan EPA opens $3 bn apparel export door with RMG push
summary:
Bangladesh aims to raise apparel exports to Japan from about $1.3-1.4 billion to $3 billion, requiring monthly shipments to roughly double. 
The 2026 EPA secures duty-free access and flexible rules of origin, boosting competitiveness. 
Success will depend on converting buyer interest into repeat orders through stronger quality, compliance, sourcing and Japan-focused execution.

title: US' Oxford Industries' Q1 sales slip 0.4% amid tariffs
summary:
Oxford Industries has reported Q1 net sales of $391 million, broadly flat YoY, while adjusted EPS declined to $1.39 due to $11 million in additional tariff costs. 
Tommy Bahama delivered growth, but Lilly Pulitzer and Johnny Was sales weakened. 
The company narrowed its FY26 sales outlook to $1.475-1.505 billion while maintaining confidence that lower tariffs.

title: Cambodia garment exports maintain growth despite May slowdown
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports rose 5.6 per cent YoY to $4.45 billion in January-May 2026, accounting for 31.7 per cent of total exports.
Growth was driven by both knitted and woven garments, although May shipments declined 7.3 per cent.
Cotton and cotton yarn imports surged 27.1 per cent, signalling stronger demand for cotton-based apparel production.

title: Bangladesh exporters concerned over US tariff move under Section 301
summary:
The United States Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed 10–12.5 per cent tariffs on 60 countries, including Bangladesh, over forced-labour concerns after Section 301 findings. 
Exporters warn total US tariffs could reach ~44 per cent, hurting competitiveness.
Exporters are urging cooperation and capacity-building measures instead of punitive tariffs.

title: Turkiye's Mavi reports Q1 profit of $11.95 mn, sales dip 2%
summary:
Turkiye’s Mavi has reported Q1 2026 revenue of TL 12.7 billion (~$279.4 million) and net profit of TL 543 million (~$11.95 million), despite a 2 per cent decline in sales amid weaker consumer demand. 
The company posted a 19.7 per cent EBITDA margin and a TL 7 billion (~$154 million) net cash position. 
Mavi added 344,000 customers and expanded its retail network.

title: US textile, apparel imports down 12% in Jan-April; China hit hardest
summary:
US textile and apparel imports fell 12.06 per cent year on year to $31.11 billion in January-April 2026, led by a sharp decline in shipments from China.
Vietnam remained the largest supplier and expanded its market share, while Cambodia also posted strong growth.
Apparel imports dropped 11.90 per cent, reflecting shifting sourcing strategies and weaker overall import demand.

title: US AAFA publishes industry glossary of traceability terms
summary:
US AAFA has published the Global Apparel, Footwear, & Accessories Glossary of Traceability Terms to establish a common reference point for terminology used across that industry. 
The glossary will define key traceability-related terms and address terminology that may appear in existing or emerging regulations, helping to promote clarity, consistency and shared understanding across the global supply chain.

title: Humana Apparels boosts capacity 15% with Coats Digital solution
summary:
Bangladesh-based Humana Apparels has improved operational efficiency after implementing Coats Digital’s FastReactPlan solution. 
The outerwear manufacturer achieved a 15 per cent increase in capacity utilisation, an 8 per cent productivity gain and a 5 per cent improvement in on-time delivery performance. 
Real-time planning and synchronised production processes reduced idle time.

title: China Cambodia AEO pact drives 1.97 bn fabric lane for apparel surge
summary:
The Cambodia-China AEO mutual-recognition pact is expected to streamline customs procedures and improve apparel supply-chain efficiency. 
With China supplying nearly $1.97 billion of textile inputs to Cambodia in January-April 2026, faster clearance and fewer inspections could support garment exports. 
The deal affirms the importance of customs trust and trade facilitation in apparel competitiveness.
